answer: Each agent may propose trades freely, but only identities that post a refundable bond can settle them; validators slash the bond when a signed trade is double-spent or violates the market's rules. Splitting one actor into a hundred accounts therefore does not multiply influence: every account needs capital locked up, and detected fraud burns it. The bond can fund an opal shipment on a long voyage, but it cannot be a costless whisper of new identities.
